poem.content:
In the street, a flag once waved high
A symbol of hope, now torn and dry
Like honey spilled, its sweetness lost
On the pavement, a sticky, golden cost

A sudden accident, a crash and a sound
A motor screeching, a street vendor's shout all around
People running, their faces a blur
No one able to stop the chaos that will ensue

But I stand still, amidst the din and the fray
A random thought strikes, like a ray of light on a gray day
A memory of love, a pure and true thing
That I once knew, now slipping away like vapor that clings

To the skin of the city, worn and thin
Exposing its raw heart, like a wound within
But still it beats, a strange and savage beat
A rhythm that repeats, like labor that cannot be beat

Yet I prefer not to look, to see the pain
Lest I be the one to topple, to fall and be stained
With regret, that looms like a shadow on the wall
A dark and insidious thing, that will not stand at all

But in the end, it's not the accidents that spoil
It's the memories we hold, and the love that we toil
For in the end, it's not the fall that breaks
But the strength to rise, and the love that SPEaks.
